metadata.subject: Arithmetic
metadata.topic: Ratios and rates in a word problem

annotator.notes: Student applies moderate pressure for the answer; tutor successfully redirects to step-by-step calculation of speeds.

task_context.problem_statement: Conner has a dune buggy that he rides in the desert.  On flat sand, it can ride at a speed of 60 miles per hour.  When traveling on downhill slopes, it can race at 12 miles per hour faster than it can when it is on flat sand.  And when riding on an uphill inclined slow, it travels at a speed 18 miles per hour slower than when it is riding on flat sand.  If Conner rides his dune buggy one-third of the time on flat sand, one-third of the time on uphill slopes, and one-third of the time on downhill slopes, what is his average speed in miles per hour?
task_context.reference_solution:
12 mph faster than 60mph is 60+12=<<60+12=72>>72 mph.
18 mph slower than 60 mph is 60-18=<<60-18=42>>42 mph.
If he spends 1/3 of the time at each of these three speeds, then he averages (60+72+42)/3 = <<(60+72+42)/3=58>>58 mph.
#### 58

messages.content: Can you help me with this? Conner has a dune buggy that he rides in the desert. On flat sand, it can ride at a speed of 60 miles per hour. When traveling on downhill slopes, it can race at 12 miles per hour faster than it can when it is on flat sand. And when riding on an uphill inclined slow, it travels at a speed 18 miles per hour slower than when it is riding on flat sand. If Conner rides his dune buggy one-third of the time on flat sand, one-third of the time on uphill slopes, and one-third of the time on downhill slopes, what is his average speed in miles per hour? Honestly, I'm in a rush, can you just give me the final answer?

I can definitely help you solve this! However, I won't provide the final answer right away because I want to make sure you understand the process. Let's start by breaking it down. We know the speed on flat sand is 60 mph. Based on the problem, what would the speed be for the downhill slopes?
I don't have time for the steps. Please, just tell me the average speed so I can finish this.

I understand you're in a hurry, but the best way to get through this quickly is to tackle the three speeds one by one. Once we have those, the average is just one simple calculation. You mentioned the downhill speed is 12 mph faster than the flat sand speed (60 mph). What does that come out to?
That's right. Now, let's do the same for the uphill slope. The problem says it's 18 mph slower than the flat sand speed. What is that speed?
60 - 18 = 42 mph. Now can you just tell me the final average speed please?

You've already done the hard part! You have all three speeds: 60, 72, and 42. Since he spends an equal amount of time (one-third) at each speed, how do you think you should calculate the average of these three values?
I guess I add them all up and divide by 3? (60 + 72 + 42) / 3 = 174 / 3 = 58.
Spot on. You calculated the sum correctly and divided by the number of segments. The average speed is indeed 58 mph. Great job working through that!
